In our commitment to open town meeting, Hingham remains true to a wonderful tradition – a tradition that allows each registered voter to play a pivotal role in the governance of the town and to do so with “voice and vote”. Town meeting is not only a gathering of citizens to consider matters of common concern; it is the legislative body of the town. As such, the meeting must be conducted in a fair and open manner and in accordance with the Town Bylaws, as well as traditions that we have followed in Hingham town meetings for many years. Several matters of procedure are summarized below.  An article in the warrant states a question for the town meeting to answer. A motion is a proposed answer to the question and must be within the scope of the article. An article (once published in the warrant) may not be amended, but a motion may be amended by vote of the meeting. All motions must be seconded.  If the Advisory Committee is recommending an affirmative motion under an article, its motion will be received as the main motion under the article. A voter may propose to amend this motion, either to change it in part or to substitute a whole new motion (sometimes called a "substitute motion"). In any such case, the proposed amendment will be taken up and voted on first and then the main motion, as it may have been amended, will be acted upon.  If the Advisory Committee is recommending no action under an article and a voter offers an affirmative motion, the voter's motion will be received as the main motion under the article. Such a motion is likewise subject to amendment.  All motions and proposed amendments involving the expenditure of money must be in writing. So must all other motions and proposed amendments unless they are so brief and simple as to be easily understood when stated orally (e.g., motion for the previous question, motion to adjourn). Voters are welcome to seek the assistance of counsel for the Town in preparing motions or proposed amendments.  Limits on speaking: No one may speak on any subject for more than six (6) minutes for the first time or for more than three (3) minutes for the second time. No one may speak more than twice on any question unless all others who have not spoken on the question shall have spoken if they desire to do so and unless leave of the meeting is first obtained. A person may speak more than twice, but only to make a brief correction of an error in or misunderstanding of his or her previous statement, including brief answers to questions from the floor (addressed through the Moderator).  In addressing the meeting, a speaker shall confine his or her remarks to the matter before the meeting.  Persons who are not registered voters of the Town may be admitted to the meeting as guests by the Moderator. A guest of the meeting may be granted permission to address the meeting by majority vote.  The purpose of the motion for the previous question is to end discussion and have an immediate vote on the pending question. The motion is not debatable and requires a majority vote for adoption. The Moderator will decline to accept a motion for the previous question if 2 other voters are seeking recognition and if both sides have not had a fair opportunity to be heard. The Moderator will accept the motion for the previous question if it appears that both sides have been heard and the discussion is becoming repetitious.  Voting procedures: All votes are taken in the first instance by voice vote. If the Moderator is in doubt as to the results or if seven (7) voters rise and express doubt as to the result declared by the Moderator, a standing vote is taken, except that a ballot vote is taken (instead of a standing vote) if either the Advisory Committee or fifty (50) voters promptly call for a ballot vote. As a ballot vote takes considerable time, our practice has been not to request a ballot vote in the absence of compelling reasons.  At a Special Town Meeting, no money may be appropriated for any purpose if the Advisory Committee recommends against the appropriation, except by a two-thirds vote of the meeting.  No vote may be reconsidered except after a two-thirds vote on a motion to reconsider such vote. The Town acknowledges that the MSBA’s grant program is a non-entitlement, discretionary program based on need, as determined by the MSBA, and any Project costs the Town incurs in excess of any grant approved by and received from the MSBA shall be the sole responsibility of the Town. Any grant that the Town may receive from the MSBA for the Project shall not exceed the lesser (1) thirty six, and eighty-nine hundredths’ percent (36.89%) of eligible, approved Project costs, as determined by the MSBA, or (2) the total maximum grant amount determined by the MSBA, or act on anything relating thereto? (Inserted at the request of the 2025 School Building Committee) COMMENT: This Article seeks authorization to fund the replacement of the roof systems at South Elementary School (“South”). The existing roof systems are of varying ages and conditions and have required repairs and maintenance over time; much of the system has reached the end of its useful life. Recently, water infiltration from ice dams required an emergency response. The proposed Project is being developed in conjunction with the Massachusetts School Building Authority (“MSBA”) Accelerated Repair Program. Background South was constructed in 1948. The school roof is approximately 57,000 square feet. The building underwent an extensive expansion and renovation in 1998 at which point the school’s roofing systems were also completely replaced. Since that time the district has maintained it mainly through targeted repairs, with an emergency repair performed as recently as summer 2025. A 2022 study performed by Habeeb & Associates, the Town’s professional consultants, found that most of the 13 sections of the roofing (and the associated drainage fixtures) needed repair, and noted that the roof systems had exceeded their 20-year warranty. The report further noted that all roofing sections were approaching the end of their standard 25-year life expectancy and thus should be replaced in the near to intermediate term. As part of this roof Project Habeeb & Associates has been contracted to conduct a peer review of all design materials being submitted through the MSBA process. 2025 Annual Town Meeting authorized $320,000 for a schematic design study for the anticipated roofing systems replacement. The Town was subsequently accepted into the MSBA Accelerated Repair Program, and an Owner’s Project Manager was selected by the MSBA. All six public school buildings are actively required to accommodate current and projected student enrollment, based on Hingham Public Schools' facility evaluations and long-term planning. Overall enrollment is experiencing an increase, and over the next 10 years, elementary enrollments are projected by New England School Development Council (“NESDEC”) to increase by 304 students. 5 Building Study and Design Process To-Date Following the Town's acceptance into the MSBA's Accelerated Repair Program, the Project's design consultant, Gale Associates (“Gale”), was engaged to evaluate the roof and develop a schematic design. The April, 2026, evaluation included a visual assessment of the roofing and flashing; limited exploratory openings; hazardous-material sampling; an infrared drone survey; and a structural feasibility study. A related Massachusetts Architectural Access Board (“MAAB”) evaluation was subsequently conducted in early May, 2026. A whole roof system assessment study found that many portions of the South roof sub-structure are sound. Original timber framing installed in 1948, does not meet current snow-load Building Code (“Code”) requirements, and requires structural augmentation. In addition, several framing members in the 1998 expansion are very close to their maximum capacity (98%), and Gale recommended structural augmentation for that portion of the building as well. The remaining portions of the roof framing and decks are generally capable of supporting current code-required loads, although several framing members require reinforcement due to insufficient capacity for the additional load of future solar panels. Although the Town is not obligated to install solar panels, under the MSBA grant program, the roof structure must have a designated solar-ready area with sufficient capacity to support solar panels. The evaluation further found that most of the asphalt shingle and low-slope membrane roofing areas are more than 20 years old and showing signs of deterioration, including damaged shingles, poor-condition roof coatings, previous repairs related to water infiltration, and deteriorated flashing, sealants, and masonry. While the existing standing-seam metal roofing is generally serviceable, replacing it as part of the Project would provide a uniform, warrantable, and betterinsulated roof system. Limited hazardous-material testing found no asbestos in the samples collected, although additional testing will be required as the project progresses. Lead-based paint was identified on a roof truss, and the Project budget includes an allowance for potential abatement of both asbestos and lead. Lower-cost coating and overlay options for the existing roofing systems were also considered. These options were not recommended because they would not address the underlying deterioration and would require continued maintenance and repairs. The study concluded that continued patching and repairs would not provide a durable, long-term solution. The recommended approach is to replace the roof systems and address related flashing, masonry and drainage problems at the same time. Following Gale’s review, roof-covering options and cost comparisons were reviewed with Hingham Public Schools and the 2025 School Building Committee (“SBC”) in public meetings in June 2026. The SBC voted to proceed with PVC membrane roofing on the low-slope areas and standing-seam metal panels on the steep-slope areas. That direction, combined with findings on the age and condition of the existing systems, culminated in a Schematic Design submitted to the MSBA on August 27, 2026, and revised on September 18, 2026; this Schematic Design is the basis for the scope and cost estimate presented in this Article. Proposed Project The proposed Project will replace the existing roofing systems down to the roof decks, with the decks inspected and repaired as needed. The work will include new low-slope and steep-slope 6 roofing systems, along with related improvements to roof edges, flashing, drainage, gutters and downspouts, and rooftop equipment. The Project will also include reinforcement of selected roof framing and related interior work to meet current Code requirements and support potential future solar installation in the designated areas. Because the proposed roof assemblies will be thicker than the existing assemblies, related modifications will be required to drainage, roof-edge and flashing systems, as well as portions of the masonry. The work will also include masonry repairs, replacement of deteriorated sealants, and replacement or modification of existing roof ladders and other roof-access components. Because the Project cost exceeds 30% of the building’s assessed value, the Project must address accessibility throughout the building, not just in areas directly affected by the roof work. Thus, the Project will include accessibility improvements identified through a review of the school for compliance with applicable MAAB requirements. The preliminary scope includes modifications to toilet-room accessories, door hardware, portions of the exterior ramp and sidewalk, handrails, signage, vestibule flooring, doors and thresholds, and water coolers. Proposed Project Cost Based on the current Schematic Design, the total Project cost is $8,576,727, an increase from the $5,400,000 estimate presented at the 2025 Annual Town Meeting. The study and evaluation of the existing roof identified additional needs, most notably the augmentation of the wood-framed roof and structural steel trusses. The expanded scope was not contemplated in the previous estimate and has been incorporated into the current Project cost. Furthermore, Project costs have increased significantly over the past two years, reflecting continued construction cost escalation and broader inflationary pressures affecting labor and materials. MUNICIPAL FINANCE TERMS APPROPRIATION – An authorization by the Town Meeting to make obligations and payments from the treasury for a specific purpose. ASSESSED VALUATION – A valuation set upon real or personal property by the Board of Assessors as a basis for levying taxes. BETTERMENT – A betterment assessment is a charge for the cost of public improvements, which benefit a limited area, against real estate situated in such. BAN – “Bond Anticipatory Note”. Short term borrowing done in advance of long term borrowing via issuance of a BOND. BANs are issued to be able to fund a project while waiting to go to formal bonding. BOND – A loan, typically over a year in maturity. BOND AUTHORIZATION – The amount of money the Town Meeting approves for borrowing for a specific purpose. BOND / BAN PREMIUM – Funds paid to the Town by financial institutions as commissions on the sale of the Town’s BONDS or BANs. These premiums are allowed under the Massachusetts Municipal Act of 2016 under Chapter 44, section 20 to be used to fund similar Capital Projects to the projects funded by the original BOND/BAN. BOND ISSUE – Generally, the sale of a certain number of bonds at one time by a governmental unit. CAPITAL BUDGET – A plan of proposed capital outlays and the means of financing them for the current fiscal period. CAPITAL OUTLAY – An expenditure for the purchase of property or equipment and for the construction or renovation of a facility and infrastructure. CHERRY SHEET – A form showing all state and county charges and reimbursements to the town as certified by the Massachusetts Department of Revenue. DEBT SERVICE – Payment of interest and repayment of principal to holders of the town’s debt instruments. ENTERPRISE FUND – Financing of services where all or most of the costs are paid for by users. ENTERPRISE RETAINED EARNINGS – If during a fiscal year an Enterprise fund produces a surplus, such surplus shall be kept in a separate account called “retained earnings”. The Department of Revenue then certifies that surplus as an available fund which can be used for: 1. operating costs to offset the need to increase user charges, 2. to fund capital improvements, 3. to reimburse General Fund to the extent the General Fund has funded a particular service in prior years, or 4. to fund Enterprise Fund revenue deficits. FISCAL YEAR - A 12-month period, commencing on July 1, to which the annual budget applies. (Abbreviated as "FY".) FREE CASH - The excess of assets over liabilities, minus uncollected taxes of prior years, also referred to as "available cash". The amount is certified annually by the Massachusetts Department of Revenue. Free Cash may be appropriated by vote of a town meeting. GENERAL FUND - The major town owned fund which is created with town receipts and which is charged with expenditures payable from such revenues. GRANT - A contribution of assets by one governmental unit or other organization to another. Typically, these contributions are made to local governments from the state and federal government. Grants are usually made for specific purposes. LEVY LIMIT - The amount of dollars a Town can raise by taxation under Proposition 2 1/2. LINE-ITEM BUDGET - A format of budgeting which organizes costs by type of expenditure. Such as expenses, equipment, and salaries. OVERLAY - The overlay is the amount raised by the Assessors to be used for potential abatement of property taxes. The Overlay Surplus is the portion of each year's overlay account no longer required to cover property tax abatements. PROPERTY TAX LEVY - The amount produced by multiplying the assessed valuation of property by the tax rate. The tax rate is expressed "per thousand dollars" of assessed valuation. RESERVE FUND - Money set aside by Town Meeting to be allocated by the Advisory Board for extraordinary and unforeseen expenditures. REVOLVING FUND (Ch.44, Sec. 53E 1/2) - A Town may annually authorize the use of a revolving fund by accounting for separately the receipts received from a particular service or program and expend from such fund for providing such service or program without appropriation. STABILIZATION FUND - A special account which is invested until used and can only be utilized by town meeting appropriation.
